gloss: A place where planes take off and land, with buildings for passengers.

The *airplane* was still sitting at the gate.

gloss: An airplane, in everyday speech.

gloss: A building at an airport or station where passengers arrive and leave.

gloss: The long strip of pavement where planes take off and land.

Ice closed both *runways* that morning.
The plane turned onto the *runway* and picked up speed.

gloss: The front section of a plane where the pilots sit.

Modern *cockpits* have almost no paper charts left.

gloss: The moment when a plane leaves the ground.

gloss: A wait between two flights on the same trip.

gloss: A short stay in a city on the way to your final destination.

gloss: A period of waiting caused by something being late.

gloss: The moving belt at an airport where checked bags come out.

gloss: A strap that holds you in your seat on a plane or in a car.

gloss: The document that lets you get on a plane.

Our *boarding passes* are saved on my phone.

gloss: A room that is free for someone to rent.

gloss: A comfortable waiting room at an airport or hotel.

The hotel has two *lounges* off the lobby.

gloss: The tired, confused feeling you get after flying across time zones.

gloss: The act of passing through a place on the way somewhere else, or public transportation as a system.

gloss: Official permission stamped in a passport to enter a country.

gloss: A place where officials stop people to inspect them or their documents.

gloss: An official paper allowing you to do something.

gloss: The legal status of belonging to a particular country.

gloss: The office of a country's chief representative in a foreign capital.

gloss: A government office in a foreign city that helps its citizens and issues visas.

gloss: A period of being kept apart from others to stop disease from spreading.

gloss: A paper or digital pass that lets you travel or enter a place.

gloss: An arrangement to hold a room, seat, or table for you.

gloss: An arrangement made in advance to buy travel or a room.

gloss: A printed slip that can be exchanged for goods or a service.

Our tour price includes hotel *vouchers*.

gloss: A written plan of where you will go and when during a trip.

gloss: The place you are traveling to.

gloss: The money you pay to ride a bus, train, taxi, or plane.

gloss: The business of providing travel and vacations for visitors.

gloss: A short vacation, usually somewhere relaxing.

gloss: A trip to see or photograph wild animals, especially in Africa.

gloss: A vacation spent traveling on a large ship that stops at several ports.

gloss: A long trip by sea or through space.

gloss: A long walk in the country or mountains.

The park has *hikes* for every level.

gloss: The activity of walking long distances in the countryside.

gloss: A traveler who goes cheaply from place to place carrying a large pack.

gloss: A building where travelers pay to stay overnight.

gloss: A roadside hotel where you park right outside your room.

gloss: Cheap lodging where travelers sleep in shared rooms.

gloss: A hotel or place built for vacations, with pools, restaurants, and activities.

gloss: A hotel or large cabin in the mountains, woods, or a park.

The *lodge* has a huge stone fireplace.

gloss: A large comfortable house, often rented for a vacation.

The *villas* sit on a hillside above the bay.

gloss: A small private house that rents rooms to travelers.

gloss: The desk or area in a hotel where guests check in.

gloss: A hotel worker who carries guests' bags to their rooms.

gloss: A person paid to carry luggage at a station, airport, or hotel.

gloss: The hotel staff and service that clean the rooms.

gloss: A small refrigerator of drinks and snacks in a hotel room.

gloss: The time or act of leaving a hotel and paying at the end of a stay.

gloss: The act of registering on arrival at a hotel or airport.

gloss: A feature or service that makes a place more comfortable.

gloss: A spot where you set up a tent or park a camper.

gloss: A structure built to remember a person or an event.
examples: A stone *monument* stands in the square.
The park is full of war *monuments*.
They laid flowers at the *monument*.

gloss: A room or building where art is shown or sold.
examples: There's a small *gallery* above the bookstore.
We spent the afternoon walking through the *galleries*.
The *gallery* is free on Sunday mornings.

gloss: A very large and important church.
examples: The *cathedral* took two hundred years to build.
We visited three *cathedrals* in one week.
You can hear the *cathedral* bells from our room.

gloss: A large old building with thick walls, built for defense.
examples: The *castle* sits on a hill above the river.
Ruined *castles* are everywhere in that valley.
Tickets to the *castle* are twelve euros.
contrast: The t is silent: KAS-uhl, not KAST-uhl.

gloss: A grand house where a ruler lives or once lived.
examples: The *palace* gardens are open to the public.
Both *palaces* were built in the same century.
We toured the *palace* with an audio guide.

gloss: What is left standing of an old destroyed building.
examples: We hiked up to the *ruins* at sunrise.
The *ruins* date from the second century.
Only a few *ruins* remain of the old fort.
contrast: In this sense the word is used only in the plural: the ruins, not a ruin.

gloss: A holy place devoted to a saint, god, or memory.
examples: Pilgrims come to the *shrine* every August.
Small *shrines* stand along the mountain path.
The *shrine* is at the top of the steps.

gloss: A building where Muslims gather to pray.
examples: The blue *mosque* is the city's main sight.
There are dozens of *mosques* in the old quarter.
Cover your head before entering the *mosque*.
contrast: The -que is a plain sk sound: MAHSK.

gloss: A structure that shoots water into the air, usually for decoration.
examples: Meet me by the *fountain* in the square.
The *fountains* are turned off in winter.
Tourists throw coins into the *fountain*.

gloss: An open public square in a town or city.
examples: The band played in the main *plaza*.
Cafes surround both *plazas*.
Kids were kicking a ball around the *plaza*.

gloss: A structure built to carry a road or path over water or a gap.
examples: The *bridge* is closed for repairs.
Seven *bridges* cross the river downtown.
You get the best view from the middle of the *bridge*.

gloss: A place that people come to see or enjoy.
examples: The falls are the biggest *attraction* in the state.
Most of the *attractions* are within walking distance.
That museum is a major tourist *attraction*.

gloss: The right to enter a place, or the price you pay to enter.
examples: *Admission* is fifteen dollars for adults.
Children under six get free *admission*.
The ticket includes *admission* to both floors.

gloss: An object or display shown to the public in a museum.
examples: The dinosaur *exhibit* is on the second floor.
New *exhibits* open every few months.
That *exhibit* was the best part of the museum.
contrast: The h is silent and the x sounds like gz: ig-ZIB-it.

gloss: A public show of art or other objects, usually for a limited time.
examples: The photography *exhibition* runs through May.
Two traveling *exhibitions* are here this summer.
We stood in line an hour for the *exhibition*.
contrast: The h is silent here too, but the x sounds like ks: ek-suh-BISH-uhn.

gloss: A high spot with a view, usually with a place to park.
examples: Pull over at the next *overlook*.
There are three *overlooks* along the canyon road.
We watched the sunset from the *overlook*.
contrast: The noun stresses the first syllable, OH-vur-luuk; the verb stresses the last, oh-vur-LUUK.

gloss: A person who shows visitors around a place and explains it.
examples: Our *guide* spoke perfect English.
The park hires *guides* for the summer season.
Ask the *guide* how old the church is.

gloss: A book of information for travelers visiting a place.
examples: I read the *guidebook* on the plane.
Old *guidebooks* list restaurants that closed years ago.
The *guidebook* said the market opens at six.

gloss: A thin printed booklet advertising a place or service.
examples: The hotel *brochure* made the pool look bigger.
There's a rack of *brochures* by the front door.
She grabbed a *brochure* about the boat tours.

gloss: A drawing of an area that shows roads, towns, and features.
examples: The desk clerk gave us a free *map*.
I still keep paper *maps* in the car.
The *map* doesn't show that road at all.

gloss: A stiff card with a picture on one side, mailed without an envelope.
examples: She sent me a *postcard* from Lisbon.
I bought six *postcards* at the museum shop.
The *postcard* arrived two weeks after she got home.

gloss: A large container of water built for swimming.
examples: The kids were in the *pool* all afternoon.
The resort has three *pools* and a hot tub.
Our room looks right out over the *pool*.

gloss: A place offering massages, baths, and beauty treatments.
examples: She booked a massage at the hotel *spa*.
Mountain towns here are full of *spas*.
The *spa* opens at eight in the morning.

gloss: A very hot wooden room used for sweating and relaxing.
examples: There's a *sauna* next to the locker room.
The gym has separate *saunas* for men and women.
Ten minutes in the *sauna* was plenty for me.

gloss: A person paid to watch swimmers and rescue anyone in trouble.
examples: The *lifeguard* blew her whistle at us.
There are no *lifeguards* on duty after six.
Swim near the *lifeguard* stand.

gloss: A short tube that lets you breathe while your face is in the water.
examples: Rent a mask and a *snorkel* at the beach hut.
The *snorkels* come with the boat tour.
Water kept getting into my *snorkel*.

gloss: A long narrow board you stand on to ride ocean waves.
examples: He strapped the *surfboard* to the roof of the car.
*Surfboards* rent for twenty dollars a day.
Her *surfboard* is shorter than mine.

gloss: Darker skin from spending time in the sun.
examples: She came back from Florida with a deep *suntan*.
Their *suntans* faded by October.
He got a *suntan* just sitting on the boat.

gloss: A small stand or self-service machine where things are sold or printed.
examples: Print your ticket at the *kiosk* by the door.
All four *kiosks* were out of order.
We bought water from a *kiosk* on the corner.

gloss: A thief who steals from people's pockets and bags in crowds.
examples: A *pickpocket* took his wallet on the subway.
Watch out for *pickpockets* around the station.
The *pickpocket* was gone before anyone noticed.

gloss: A raised wooden path built along a beach for people to walk on.
examples: We walked the whole *boardwalk* after dinner.
Old *boardwalks* run along both beaches.
There's an ice cream stand at the end of the *boardwalk*.
